articles.title: F1 2026 calendar: Race schedule, highlights, results, Sprint venues, driver line-ups, new regulations, live Sky Sports coverage
articles.summary: All the key dates, driver line-ups, teams and changes you need to know about with Formula 1 in 2026; watch all 22 race weekends live on Sky Sports F1 and the Sky Sports app once again in 2026
articles.body:
Here's a look at all you need to know about the 2026 Formula 1 season as Lando Norris defends his world title.

The season will now feature 22 rounds following the cancellation of the Bahrain and Saudi Arabian Grands Prix in April due to the Middle East conflict. The 2026 campaign started in Australia in early March and runs through to Abu Dhabi on December 4-6.

There will be a new track on the calendar in the form of Madrid in September, as the drivers will race around the streets of the Spanish capital, while Imola has dropped off the schedule.

  • Got Sky? Watch F1 races LIVE on your phone! 📱
  • Not got Sky? Get Sky Sports or stream with no contract on NOW 📺
  • Choose the sports notifications you want! 🔔

The biggest change is the regulations as new technical rules mean we will see new cars and a likely shaken-up pecking order throughout the season.

American manufacturer Cadillac will join the grid, so there will be 11 teams for the first time since 2016 and Britain's Arvid Lindblad is the only rookie in the field.

F1 2026 calendar

F1 2026 Sprint venues

The 2026 F1 driver line-ups

McLaren: Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri

Mercedes: George Russell and Kimi Antonelli

Red Bull: Max Verstappen and Isack Hadjar

Ferrari: Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton

Williams: Carlos Sainz and Alex Albon

Racing Bulls: Liam Lawson and Arvid Lindblad

Aston Martin: Fernando Alonso and Lance Stroll

Haas: Esteban Ocon and Oliver Bearman

Audi: Nico Hulkenberg and Gabriel Bortoleto

Alpine: Pierre Gasly and Franco Colapinto

Cadillac: Sergio Perez and Valtteri Bottas

New F1 regulations in 2026

The big change in 2026 will be a complete overhaul of the technical regulations that will see major changes to the power unit, chassis and aerodynamic rules. The cars will be very different to say the least.

New car design rules in F1 almost certainly causes a shake-up to the pecking order. Sky Sports F1's Martin Brundle has described the new regulations as the "biggest changes ever" in the sport.

The teams have long been working on their 2026 cars because the regulations are scheduled to be in place for five seasons. Being quick from this season will set you up to be competitive for the years to come. Mercedes' dominance in 2014, for example, lasted until 2016 before they were finally caught by Ferrari and Red Bull.

There will be no more DRS, instead we will have "Overtake Mode" where the drivers can use more power on designated straights if they are within one second of another car. We will also see "Active Aero" which means the front and rear wings will be moving before and after corners.

Different deployment strategies are expected, so we could see drivers attacking in unusual places which will create a variation in overtaking opportunities.

articles.title: British GP: Martin Brundle on 'immense' Silverstone 2026, Charles Leclerc's win and a Safety Car rule he'd change
articles.summary: Sky Sports F1's Martin Brundle provides the definitive final word on a breathless Silverstone weekend, assessing Kimi Antonelli's speed to win the Sprint, Charles Leclerc's turnaround to end his race victory drought, and offers his suggestions for a regulation he would like to see revised
articles.body:
Silverstone's British Grand Prix 2026 was an immense event, and it could have been truly epic without a regulation which I have been complaining about for years.

There were officially 564,000 event spectators, and of course fans who were there all weekend were counted more than once, but there was an impressive 175,000 present on race day, and each and every one I met, or saw, were cheering and smiling. It was quite the festival.

Even the weather was great, which always pleases me as it silences my international friends in the paddock who enjoy mocking our green but often wet and chilly land.

  • F1 2026 standings | F1 2026 Calendar | F1 Gossip Column
  • Download the Sky Sports app for expert analysis, best video & more📱
  • Not got Sky? Get Sky Sports or stream with no contract on NOW📺

Being a Sprint weekend, it was flat out all the way for everyone involved in F1, and totally relentless, but that really does energise every track session.

Teams and drivers know that a championship can be won or lost by a few points, such as last year, and so they all count even if the Sprint only offers a total of eight points.

'You've got to love the make-up of our current F1 grid'

The start of the Sprint was wild. With just 17 laps available, all the drivers were using overtaking boost and opportunities with relish. I remember the 80's turbo cars when it was so tempting and effective to use the readily available boost button on the steering wheel and then worrying about the fuel consumption deficit later.

'Don't use the overtake boost button' is a bit like saying 'don't think of a pink elephant'. You simply must.

Once all the side-by-side action settled down the drivers had to stabilise their batteries and electrical deployment for a few laps and drive with more control and purpose. Out front it became a two-horse race between Lewis Hamilton's Ferrari and Kimi Antonelli's Mercedes.

You've got to love the make-up of our current F1 grid, the teenager who took over the seven-time champ's Merc seat in wheel-to-wheel combat, 21 years between their ages.

Eventually Antonelli, who seems so good in the second half of any stint on a set of Pirelli tyres, had Hamilton on the ropes out of the Loop Turn 4, down the Wellington Straight and into Brooklands Turn 6.

Lewis has used some battery to defend, Kimi maturely bided his time and used overtake mode and all the tools available to pass for the lead down the Hangar Straight. The resulting breeze past was so powerful with a 25mph advantage it was a bit painful to witness. It was Antonelli's first Sprint victory.

Lando Norris would put in a fine drive, on a weekend when McLaren were really struggling for pace, for the final Sprint podium slot. George Russell was fourth and, intriguingly, Charles Leclerc a distant fifth in the other Ferrari.

Max Verstappen seemed unhappy with his car's speed and handling pretty much all weekend but was able to extract a time when it mattered. Isack Hadjar often looked marginally faster in the other Red Bull and indeed would go on to outqualify Max for the main race.

The Racing Bulls lads, Liam Lawson and Arvid Lindblad, are having a great time as fifth-fastest team and bringing home the points.

Lawson would score in both races, and Lindblad scored on his British GP debut with a fine seventh place in Sunday's GP. Impressive all round for that team, now just one point behind Alpine in the Constructors' Championship, who also had two drivers, Pierre Gasly and Franco Colapinto, in the GP points in ninth and 10th.

Leclerc's turnaround and the lesson learned for Antonelli after 'heartbreak'

Leclerc had some kind of lightbulb moment after the Sprint in terms of car set-up and particularly driving style for these quirky 2026 cars. He would qualify his Ferrari on the front row of the grid for Sunday's main event, beaten only by the irrepressible Antonelli.

A great start for both Ferraris would put Leclerc in the lead followed by third-place starter Hamilton in the other Prancing Horse up to second. Antonelli sensibly slotted into third, he had a championship lead to protect and enough speed and confidence to make amends over the next 52 laps.

Leclerc was driving beautifully out front, Hamilton less happy with his Ferrari race car on full fuel tanks and longer runs. Antonelli would once again eventually hunt him down and pass, but the gap to Leclerc out front would then only marginally reduce each lap.

Ferrari pitted Hamilton on lap 23 for new hard compound tyres, and Mercedes pitted Russell on the same lap. Leclerc would pit from the lead on lap 25, but critically Antonelli could carry decent speed until Mercedes pitted him a full 10 laps later giving him a very significant tyre advantage over Leclerc.

To put that in perspective, Verstappen and Norris would make their second tyre stops just three laps later. Antonelli was catching Leclerc hand over fist, and it seemed inevitable he would win the race, until he radioed in and then slowed on lap 41 with steering issues.

Part of his aero bodywork around the left-front wheel had failed on the serrated kerb on the outside of the high-speed Copse corner.

It was heartbreaking for him, but another lesson learned as he did not give clear enough information on his way into the pits about his problems. The team changed the easy and fast parts with a new nose and front wing, and fresh tyres, and sent him out, but the offending bodywork was still blocking his steering and he had to pit again two laps later.

Kimi persevered and, still in 10th place with a potentially critical one point in his pocket, he found remarkable pace again and carried on.

But with his issues he had been off the track five times and was given a five-second penalty for 'track limits'. That rule needs adjusting, track limit penalties are for when drivers gain a competitive advantage by cutting corners or running wide and so able to carry more speed. They should not be applied when you're surviving a mechanical issue or getting out of the way.

Nonetheless his pace was such that he would have cycled through the penalty and still finished ahead of the two Alpines, until lap 48 when Verstappen's rear wing didn't close properly to re-establish full downforce and, for the second time in eight days, albeit apparently for slightly different reasons, spun him off the track.

He was a long way into the gravel at the fast Stowe corner, having driven a great race in chasing down Hamilton's second-placed Ferrari, and a full safety car was understandably called.

Ferrari pitted Leclerc and Hamilton to give them a reasonably fresh set of soft compound tyres for the restart…

Russell had cruelly attracted a slow puncture after a feisty drive and had to make an unscheduled stop on lap 34. At that point it felt once again that if George didn't have bad luck this season, he'd have no luck at all, but that was relatively short-lived as Mercedes chose not to pit in at the safety car and he ended up with track position ahead of Hamilton and would finish in an astonishing second place given Verstappen was also now out of the race.

That's because the race never restarted, with some of the crowd rightly booing.

The 'potential fixes' for Safety Car rules

Given the current cars' enormous power with no regard for needing to have any battery left after the chequered flag, and cool tyres after the safety car period and a bunched-up pack, we were heading for an epic one-lap shoot-out.

It didn't happen. Providing it's considered safe, which on a dry sunny day with no people, debris, or stranded cars around the track it understandably was, the Race Director can allow eligible lapped cars to pass the leading pack and head off at faster but safe speed.

I believe this was inaugurated to ensure backmarkers didn't get involved and affect the result at the front of the race, and as a perceived benefit from time-to-time drivers were brought back into full contention later in the race. But the system is guaranteed to unduly prolong the safety car period, especially on long circuits like Silverstone and Spa.

I used to have robust conversations with the very sadly departed Charlie Whiting about this, because it makes no sense especially as the rules state that the safety car will recover to the pits on the lap following allowing lapped runners through. Abu Dhabi 2021 anybody?

On this occasion it transpires we were into lap 51 when the announcement was declared regarding lapped runners, and despite a massive tease that the safety car would indeed pit at the end of that lap which turned out to be an error, the race would finish at a relative snail's pace under safety car conditions.

There are potential fixes. In IndyCar for example, if it's within the last 10 laps, instead of a wave-by the lapped cars are made to peel off into the pit lane and rejoin at the back of the field. Or we could simply have the lapped runners simply drop behind the pack.

Or throw a red flag and have a standing restart in race order, although this takes a while. Instead, we prioritise runners who haven't been good enough, for whatever reason, on the day, instead of the leaders and most importantly the fans.

One caveat is, in true F1 style, defining exactly who a lapped runner is given the regulation states that it depends if they 'were lapped at the time they crossed the Line at the end of the lap during which they crossed the first safety car line for the second time after the Safety Car was deployed'.

This caught Williams and Carlos Sainz out, not least due to the pitlane geography at Silverstone where you miss out three track corners, and he was penalised by a lap after the race. We do make it hard to understand.

The 'new precedent' in Hamilton's post-race investigation

Hamilton had a yellow flag infringement hanging over him post-race and he seemed certain he would receive a penalty, which given the whole remaining pack was lined up behind the safety car would have taken him out of the points.

He received a reprimand instead because it was clear on review that he was well into the brief yellow zone before he could have possibly detected it or the yellow flag. Seeing a green light panel encourages you to get on with it but also tells you that you've must have just passed a yellow warning, however brief, and hence the reprimand.

Interestingly, and with a new precedent, given Verstappen was trying to re-overtake him, it was recognised that Hamilton was focused on one of those multiple power attacks we have in 2026, and so compromised in seeing the yellow zone or brief yellow light on his steering wheel.

A rejuvenated and relieved Leclerc won his first GP since Austin 2024, for Ferrari's 250th Grand Prix victory at the same venue as their first win back in 1951.

Russell's good fortune recovered him to second place and now just 25 points behind championship leader Antonelli, and Hamilton survived a five-second jump start penalty and the yellow flag saga for a fine third and his 16th British GP podium.

Norris would finish a solid if unspectacular fourth in front of his adoring 16,000 fans seated at the legendary Stowe corner.

And breathe. It's spectacular Spa in just under two weeks.

Formula 1's summer run continues with the Belgian Grand Prix at legendary Spa-Francorchamps on July 17-19, live on Sky Sports F1. Stream Sky Sports with NOW - no contract, cancel anytime

articles.title: Belgian GP: Martin Brundle on George Russell's problems and Lewis Hamilton clash, Kimi Antonelli's win in Spa race verdict
articles.summary: Sky Sports F1's Martin Brundle provides the final word on the talking points from Spa-Francorchamps where Kimi Antonelli re-stamped his authority on the 2026 title race and his two nearest challengers endured challenging weekends
articles.body:
The Kimi Antonelli show, also known as the 2026 Belgian Grand Prix, took place in remarkably sunny and dry conditions throughout, if occasionally interrupted by an actual safety car deployment on lap one to clear a beached car, and a few more virtual safety cars to clear up high-tech litter from the racing surface.

The Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps has been developed and polished beautifully in almost every respect, even if in time-honoured fashion getting into and moving around the venue seems to have new systems and rules every day. To be fair, there is a huge area and a great many fans to be controlled.

As usual I was out and about trackside on Friday during practice and the cars looked very fast and impressive in front of the numerous grandstands. I've been racing here for 45 years, and I couldn't quite believe my eyes on the scale of the crowd.

  • Hungarian GP: UK schedule and how to watch on Sky Sports
  • F1 2026 standings | F1 2026 calendar | F1 Gossip Column
  • Download the Sky Sports app for expert analysis, best video & more📱
  • Not got Sky? Get Sky Sports or stream with no contract on NOW📺

It was enjoyable to watch the drivers jockey an excess of power over grip through medium-speed chicane exits, but like Silverstone there was a hidden story alongside the trackside 'wow', and the drivers were very restrained through the event not to complain too much about it.

We long ago lost Eau Rouge and Raidillon as corners to refined high-downforce cars with grippy tyres and a manicured racetrack, meaning from the turn one La Source hairpin to the long haul up to the turn five Les Combes chicane is effectively a straight.

But with the need to charge the hybrid batteries on this fast track, the longest on the calendar, just as with Copse, Becketts, and Stowe at Silverstone, as the engine is used to charge those batteries the arrival speeds into corners like Pouhon at Spa are dulled such that the corner effectively becomes a bendy straight too.

On such circuits we have lost the driver-defining, and thrilling, high-speed corners. It was the same in Suzuka.

Luckily in Budapest this weekend it will not be a problem at all, and normal service will be resumed, although there are no high-speed corners worth their name.

We have known for a while about these issues, and they are being addressed where possible for 2027 and again in 2028, but the last two races have unequivocally confirmed that we need a major power unit philosophy change much sooner than later.

There were always going to be teething problems reliability-wise but as we hurtle towards the summer break the words 'deployment issues' and 'no battery' are rather too prominent.

Russell's Mercedes problems and the 'racing incident' debate

George Russell is clearly not a direct descendant of the Alessandro Volta, Michael Faraday, Thomas Edison or Nikola Tesla families because he never seems to have the right battery power at the moment.

Whether that is missing straight-line speed compared to his team-mate Antonelli in qualifying, for whatever mystery reasons, or climbing the hill to turn five on the opening lap.

Antonelli got away well at the start and Verstappen's Red Bull launched unusually nicely too. But Max appeared to pull a cunning move by powering past before Eau Rouge at the bottom of the hill, but his post-race comments say that his car had too much battery deployment suggesting he had nothing to do with that cunning plan…

Both Mercedes of Antonelli and Russell started the race with less battery charge than needed, and it particularly hurt Russell on the long climb to the critical turn five braking point, and he was mugged by three cars including Lewis Hamilton.

George braked impressively late trying to make up for his poor arrival speed and was on the outside of Lewis, leaving racing room. Lewis, close behind Max, slid a little wide and contacted George who spun into retirement, and at the same time taking a massive hit to his championship comeback chances.

More referee leeway is given on the first lap with the pack inevitably in close company along with full fuel and sub-optimal brake and tyre temperatures. I called it a racing incident in commentary, unless the stewards were satisfied that Lewis had lost control of his car, which didn't appear to be the case.

George recovered to the pits by scooter and called it a racing incident whilst far more distraught about his ongoing power issues.

Ferrari called it a racing incident, I guess you could say they would, and most people I know agreed. But with whatever extra information the stewards had they applied a five-second penalty mitigated down from the standard 10 seconds. It perhaps cost Lewis a podium but that's speculative.

Later in the race, Charles Leclerc would squeeze Oscar Piastri in the T5 braking zone and there was contact which damaged Piastri's aero parts, to an extent. For me this was a clear movement in the braking zone which can mean anything from a warning flag to a full pit-lane drive through penalty in the guidelines.

The stewards, though, decided it was about relative front axle positions and who had the right to the corner. Leclerc's telling reaction when it was played out in the cooldown room tells us everything we need to know on that one.

The pit stops that did - and didn't - make the difference

Hamilton had a torrid weekend with an accident in practice, the five-second penalty with Russell, and nearly running one of his mechanics over in the pit stop through no fault of his own. That incident attracted a team fine rather than a race penalty and so Lewis was perhaps relieved to finish fourth, probably for the first time in his life.

Piastri drove a spirited race to fifth despite his car damage although he lacked the same pace, which threatened to make the podium early on, after he swapped onto the hard compound tyres on lap 20 of 44.

Lando Norris drove beautifully all weekend but had to start 13th due to needing power unit control electronics beyond the allowance in the regulations, which is designed to keep costs down so that wealthy teams can't just throw new parts at the car every weekend.

Curiously McLaren chose not to use the virtual safety cars, or indeed a straightforward pit stop, until Lando eventually pitted on lap 30 to get rid of his starting hard-compound tyres. This left him with too much to do to catch Isack Hadjar who started his Red Bull from the back row of the grid, also due to numerous power unit penalties, to finish an impressive sixth.

Red Bull pitted Hadjar on lap one, and then again on lap two to cycle through the mandatory use of two different tyre compounds under cover of the Russell safety car, and then again under a virtual safety car on lap 20. Nicely done.

That same lap 20 VSC played out beautifully for Leclerc in his Ferrari as the time loss is only around 11 seconds when your rivals are lapping at reduced speed. Antonelli had pitted on lap 18 under full green conditions as Mercedes were covering off Red Bull's pit stop for Verstappen on lap 17.

Through all this Leclerc leapfrogged the pair of them and was now effectively leading, albeit with the yet-to-stop Norris ahead of him. Antonelli would hunt him down but perhaps not as rapidly as expected, Leclerc was driving beautifully.

'What a difference a year makes'

Eventually, and frankly inevitably given his speed throughout the event, the Italian teenager would take the lead, but Leclerc still wouldn't give up, and he finished second just two seconds adrift.

Verstappen would finish a solid third, Leclerc's safety car good fortune denied him a shot at second.

The final points went to Gabriel Bortoleto and Audi in eighth, Arvid Lindblad and Racing Bulls in ninth, and Franco Colapinto for Alpine in 10th. The safety cars played a role for and against throughout.

What a difference a year makes. Antonelli never ran higher than 14th on his F1 debut here last year, but he was in a class of one this season.

Mercedes are on fire too, with their eighth victory of the season, which is one more than they won over the last four 'ground effect era' seasons combined. That combination will take some stopping from winning both championships in fine style.

paragraphs:
The Kimi Antonelli show, also known as the 2026 Belgian Grand Prix, took place in remarkably sunny and dry conditions throughout, if occasionally interrupted by an actual safety car deployment on lap one to clear a beached car, and a few more virtual safety cars to clear up high-tech litter from the racing surface.

The Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps has been developed and polished beautifully in almost every respect, even if in time-honoured fashion getting into and moving around the venue seems to have new systems and rules every day. To be fair, there is a huge area and a great many fans to be controlled.

articles.title: Goodwood Cup: Scandinavia retains Group 1 crown after eventful race
articles.summary: Scandinavia emulated the great Kyprios when cruising home to win back-to-back Goodwood Cup crowns for Aidan O'Brien at the South Coast track; Having parted company with Hector Crouch early, Amiloc hampered runner-up Trawlerman late on, allowing the Ballydoyle horse a comfortable victory.
articles.body:
Scandinavia confirmed his superiority over Trawlerman to defend his Al Shaqab Goodwood Cup title in fine style at Goodwood.

Aidan O'Brien's son of Justify and his John and Thady Gosden-trained adversary had served up a thriller in the Gold Cup at Royal Ascot and another titanic tussle looked on the cards on the Sussex Downs.

Sent off the 6-5 favourite, Ryan Moore was always hot on the heels of Trawlerman who headed affairs in the hands of William Buick, in a race that had early drama when Amiloc unshipped Hector Crouch leaving the stalls.

Amiloc would again play a key role after Buick had set sail for home heading downhill into the straight and with the two Ascot rivals knuckling down for another battle, the loose Amiloc cut across the pair, checking Trawlerman's momentum and allowing Scandinavia to scorch clear.

  • Kalpana defeats Calandagan in King George battle
  • Kalpana wins the King George | Full replay

He galloped on eight and a half lengths into the distance as Trawlerman finished second once again to his Ballydoyle foe, with Roger Varian's Rahiebb third.

"I'm delighted, I'm thankful to everyone around him. He's a great horse, he's a real top stayer," said O'Brien.

"He's a high cruising speed, he relaxes and finds his momentum. Ryan said he finds the minute he starts asking him, he starts coming alive underneath him.

"We were a bit worried coming to Ascot because we've never been two and a half (miles) and you're never sure until you do it.

"We felt he's really gone the right way since Ascot. It's a great race to win, very prestigious.

"It's great that Trawlerman came and all the horses were there, it's what we all want to see - win, lose or draw.

"We thought that Trawlerman was going to make it, we were hoping that he would so Ryan could just follow him as he did in Ascot.

"It was going to be very simple, was he good enough or not? Obviously there was a little bit of drama, Trawlerman was a bit slowly away and Ralph's (Beckett) horse (Amiloc) was loose.

"It was a bit eventful, but it was still a great race at a great track. It was a spectacle to watch and going two miles, you get a great chance to look at it and take it in."

Of Scandinavia's future, O'Brien added: "He's very sound, he loves what he's doing and the lads love having him.

"When you get a horse like this that can race year in, year out, that's what makes it special.

"They're very hard to find, impossible really. I would imagine he'll keep racing as long as he stays safe and sound.

"He could (emulate Yeats, four-time winner of the Gold Cup), he's a natural cruiser. He's easy to train, he's a great mind and as he's by Justify, he has that great rhythm."

Moore said: "It was nice for him to have a horse to follow all the way, he probably thinks he got beat!

"His stride never shortened, he just kept galloping all the way to the line - what more can you say?

"He likes fast ground, he's a high-class horse and hopefully there's a few more good days to come."

Kaiya Fraser shines with Vintage performance

Kaiya Fraser produced a brilliant ride to land the Coral Vintage Stakes at Goodwood aboard the unbeaten Dr Rascal and celebrated the biggest victory of his career in the process.

The winning jockey had endured the nasty experience of being pulled from the saddle of the Oliver Cole-trained colt by the bite of a loose horse before remounting to win at Ascot earlier this month.

On this occasion the 23-year-old held his nerve to squeeze through a narrow gap on the rails on the inside of David Egan on Pikachu a furlong from home, delivering the son of Sottsass to land the spoils at 13-2 by half a length from the Aidan O'Brien-trained Haffner.

Favourite Al Hudaiba once again looked a difficult ride, with William Buick struggling to get him going before finishing a close third.

Fraser said: "It means everything, this is what we wake up for every morning.

"I've put so much hard work in to get where I am today and all the people around who have helped me - my agent James Forrest and all the owners and trainers who put me up.

"I'm very grateful to them and I wouldn't be here if it wasn't for them."

He added: "You saw today, he had to get a push into the stalls because he obviously had that experience last time out where he got a bit nervous, but luckily he's a willing horse and he went in with a bit of encouragement and he got out and got the job done."

This was a first victory for Cole in a race his father Paul won three times with Putra (1996), Central Park (1997) and Strategic Prince (2006).

He said: "I was always quietly confident, he's a very good horse.

"I wasn't very nervous before the race which was quite a good thing because I have a lot of faith in this horse.

"He's a very fast horse… another unlucky run really because he got loose before Ascot and then he's just got mullered coming up there in the straight and he's still won.

"We'll probably look to the Dewhurst or something like that; he's got so much class and so much speed and he's very well bred, we're very lucky to have him in our stable.

"We're not used to these kinds of horses so back to the drawing board (for plans). The Royal Lodge probably not. I'll have to go away and have a think about it.

"It means a lot (to follow in his father's footsteps). My first complete year as a trainer, it means a lot. It's not just me, there's a big group at home that work so hard - I'm very proud of all of them."

The stewards did have a look afterwards, but found Fraser and Dr Rascal had gone through a legitimate gap on the inside of Pikachu.

Fraser said: "My horse slightly came off his line and I just had to straighten him up, didn't cause anything.

"I'm delighted, first Group winner - in a Group Two on a very nice two-year-old, so I'm looking forward to the future."

articles.title: Goodwood: Bow Echo roars home late to seal Sussex success
articles.summary: The brilliant Bow Echo notched a sixth consecutive victory with a hard-fought triumph in the Sussex Stakes at Goodwood; Also on the card, Flora Of Bermuda relished the step up in trip when scoring in the Oak Tree Stakes.
articles.body:
Bow Echo’s dazzling turn of foot once again came to the fore as he came out on top in an epic renewal of the Visit Qatar Sussex Stakes.

George Boughey's unbeaten colt was a brilliant winner of the 2000 Guineas before overcoming adversity to register a workmanlike victory in the St James' Palace Stakes at Royal Ascot and was the 10-11 favourite to complete a famous hat-trick at Goodwood last achieved by the one and only Frankel in 2011.

It was again not an easy watch for odds-on backers, with Bow Echo stuck in the middle of the pack with plenty of work to do as the race began in earnest, but he ultimately went through the gears in stunning fashion in the final half-furlong to get up and beat his old rival Gstaad by half a length.

Boughey said: "He's got an explosive turn of foot, it was probably a bit messier than we might have thought with the gallop they went.

  • Scandinavia retains Goodwood Cup crown after eventful race
  • Kalpana defeats Calandagan in King George battle

"Huge credit to Billy again for being ice cool. He's an extraordinary horseman and rider to go with it and Billy producing the horse like he is is just phenomenal.

"But fundamentally what an animal. The constitution to have another rough race, relax through it then find the line as strong as he did - I'm lost for words really.

"He's so fast, he's like a motorbike. He stays the mile, but has an exceptional turn of foot to go with it. Billy has had tremendous belief in this horse for a long time and so have I.

"We knew what happened at Ascot and it was just having the confidence to take stock and go again. I always thought this was the race for him, we had to get him back from what was a hard race (at Royal Ascot), but he's shown how good he is there.

"It was always going to be messy, a Sussex Stakes with 12 runners. But it was to the letter how we wanted to ride the horse. There were a few gaps that closed and Billy had to sit tight and come round, but it was brilliant."

Emulating Frankel with his Newmarket, Ascot and Goodwood treble is an achievement that gives his handler overwhelming pride.

Boughey added: "It's not lost on me what he has achieved this year and it dawned on the last few days I might never be in this position again. There are a lot of trainers who have trained a lot better horses than I have who haven't been in this position.

"It's desperately sad Sheikh Mohammed Obaid isn't here to see him and this is 30-plus years of work to get here.

"I can't put into words what this horse means to me and he's a warrior as well as being a very fast horse."

Having delighted on home soil, he could now head on his travels.

Boughey said: "The plan was either to go to France for the Prix Jacques le Marois or the Prix du Moulin. We would love for the horse to end up in a Breeders' Cup Mile at the end of the year and I think round a bend in America off a strong pace will suit him well."

Loughnane said: "They made life difficult for him, but I always wanted to follow Ryan (Moore, on Gstaad), that was my plan.

"I knew the pace would be on with the set-up of the race. I was boxed in between Ryan and Christophe (Soumillon, on Puerto Rico) and I just had to wait to get out. But once I did, he proved how good he is."

Flora Of Bermuda finds seven furlongs to her liking

Flora Of Bermuda landed a first win over seven furlongs to open new routes in Group company when outclassing her rivals in the Rolls-Royce Oak Tree Stakes.

The Andrew Balding-trained filly had previously plied her trade almost exclusively at six furlongs, placing at Group One level and winning the Group Three Summer Stakes at York last time out.

But opportunities at both six and seven furlongs now beckon for the five-year-old after she produced a solid performance as the 5-2 favourite to land this Group Three contest by a neck from Sayidah Dariyan with Radiant Beauty third.

The Wathnan Racing-owned Flora Of Bermuda sat in sixth place as Zanthos cut out the early running but after starting to make ground at the cutaway, she took it up at the furlong pole and stayed on strongly to the line.

Balding said: "We've been thinking about seven furlongs for a bit and this seemed an obvious place to try it.

"She's been very consistent at a high level throughout her career and is a fantastic filly. She's done very well physically this year, she has to go in the stalls late and if she has any flaw it is she is not very patient, she'll go in the stalls OK but just won't stand there for any longer than 30 seconds.

"Ascot was a bit of a disaster and she fluffed the start, but other than that she is three from three this year.

"You can't really go abroad with her because of the stalls, she will probably go to the City of York Stakes or the Haydock Sprint Cup. It would be great to win a Group One with her one day and I think if everything drops right for her one time she will.

"She's amazingly versatile and won the Alice Keppel here on heavy ground and then a few years later this on fast ground."

Wild Blossom takes another step forward

Bigger and better things may await Wild Blossom after her taking victory in the British Stallion Studs EBF Alice Keppel Fillies' Conditions Stakes.

Karl Burke's Wathnan Racing-owned filly came into the race having finished 10th in the Queen Mary, although that run was better than the placing suggested as she was only beaten four and a half lengths.

Under James Doyle she was the 5-4 favourite to make good on the promise shown at Royal Ascot, and did so with little fuss, prevailing by a length and a half from Andrew Balding's Fast Track.

"She worked with a very good older filly last week and worked very nicely," said Burke.

"It is just a slight concern when they do it so well first time on slow ground, then she ran very well at Ascot where the draw completely scuppered her really.

"This was the plan since Ascot. I don't know, we'll look at all those Group five-furlong races, she's a very quick filly.

"I wouldn't dismiss six furlongs, we'll see what James says, but that was the plan.

"There's no real future targets at the moment, the Flying Childers at Doncaster, races like that."

Connections of Infraad were made to wait for confirmation of their victory in the opening Coral Rewards Shaker Handicap, but were eventually thrilled to see William Haggas' improving colt keep the race after a stewards' inquiry.

Tom Marquand's mount was sent off the 2-1 favourite and edged out Andrew Balding's well-regarded 9-4 market rival Hatteen for a head success after a late duel between the two lightly-raced three-year-olds.

Maureen Haggas, assistant to her husband, said: "You never know these days what they will do, but I could imagine it took so long because Tom and Oisin (Murphy) were in the same room and they are quite good talkers and they couldn't stop them.

"He needed every inch of the mile and a half and it would not surprise me if he goes a bit further in time. He's a work in progress and he's going the right way. He's got his act together today and hopefully he keeps progressing."
paragraphs:
Bow Echo’s dazzling turn of foot once again came to the fore as he came out on top in an epic renewal of the Visit Qatar Sussex Stakes.

George Boughey's unbeaten colt was a brilliant winner of the 2000 Guineas before overcoming adversity to register a workmanlike victory in the St James' Palace Stakes at Royal Ascot and was the 10-11 favourite to complete a famous hat-trick at Goodwood last achieved by the one and only Frankel in 2011.

It was again not an easy watch for odds-on backers, with Bow Echo stuck in the middle of the pack with plenty of work to do as the race began in earnest, but he ultimately went through the gears in stunning fashion in the final half-furlong to get up and beat his old rival Gstaad by half a length.

Boughey said: "He's got an explosive turn of foot, it was probably a bit messier than we might have thought with the gallop they went.

  • Scandinavia retains Goodwood Cup crown after eventful race
  • Kalpana defeats Calandagan in King George battle

"Huge credit to Billy again for being ice cool. He's an extraordinary horseman and rider to go with it and Billy producing the horse like he is is just phenomenal.

"But fundamentally what an animal. The constitution to have another rough race, relax through it then find the line as strong as he did - I'm lost for words really.

"He's so fast, he's like a motorbike. He stays the mile, but has an exceptional turn of foot to go with it. Billy has had tremendous belief in this horse for a long time and so have I.

"We knew what happened at Ascot and it was just having the confidence to take stock and go again. I always thought this was the race for him, we had to get him back from what was a hard race (at Royal Ascot), but he's shown how good he is there.

"It was always going to be messy, a Sussex Stakes with 12 runners. But it was to the letter how we wanted to ride the horse. There were a few gaps that closed and Billy had to sit tight and come round, but it was brilliant."

Emulating Frankel with his Newmarket, Ascot and Goodwood treble is an achievement that gives his handler overwhelming pride.

Boughey added: "It's not lost on me what he has achieved this year and it dawned on the last few days I might never be in this position again. There are a lot of trainers who have trained a lot better horses than I have who haven't been in this position.

"It's desperately sad Sheikh Mohammed Obaid isn't here to see him and this is 30-plus years of work to get here.

"I can't put into words what this horse means to me and he's a warrior as well as being a very fast horse."

Having delighted on home soil, he could now head on his travels.

Boughey said: "The plan was either to go to France for the Prix Jacques le Marois or the Prix du Moulin. We would love for the horse to end up in a Breeders' Cup Mile at the end of the year and I think round a bend in America off a strong pace will suit him well."

Loughnane said: "They made life difficult for him, but I always wanted to follow Ryan (Moore, on Gstaad), that was my plan.

"I knew the pace would be on with the set-up of the race. I was boxed in between Ryan and Christophe (Soumillon, on Puerto Rico) and I just had to wait to get out. But once I did, he proved how good he is."

Flora Of Bermuda finds seven furlongs to her liking

Flora Of Bermuda landed a first win over seven furlongs to open new routes in Group company when outclassing her rivals in the Rolls-Royce Oak Tree Stakes.

The Andrew Balding-trained filly had previously plied her trade almost exclusively at six furlongs, placing at Group One level and winning the Group Three Summer Stakes at York last time out.

But opportunities at both six and seven furlongs now beckon for the five-year-old after she produced a solid performance as the 5-2 favourite to land this Group Three contest by a neck from Sayidah Dariyan with Radiant Beauty third.

The Wathnan Racing-owned Flora Of Bermuda sat in sixth place as Zanthos cut out the early running but after starting to make ground at the cutaway, she took it up at the furlong pole and stayed on strongly to the line.

Balding said: "We've been thinking about seven furlongs for a bit and this seemed an obvious place to try it.

"She's been very consistent at a high level throughout her career and is a fantastic filly. She's done very well physically this year, she has to go in the stalls late and if she has any flaw it is she is not very patient, she'll go in the stalls OK but just won't stand there for any longer than 30 seconds.

"Ascot was a bit of a disaster and she fluffed the start, but other than that she is three from three this year.

"You can't really go abroad with her because of the stalls, she will probably go to the City of York Stakes or the Haydock Sprint Cup. It would be great to win a Group One with her one day and I think if everything drops right for her one time she will.

"I wouldn't dismiss six furlongs, we'll see what James says, but that was the plan.

"There's no real future targets at the moment, the Flying Childers at Doncaster, races like that."

Connections of Infraad were made to wait for confirmation of their victory in the opening Coral Rewards Shaker Handicap, but were eventually thrilled to see William Haggas' improving colt keep the race after a stewards' inquiry.

Tom Marquand's mount was sent off the 2-1 favourite and edged out Andrew Balding's well-regarded 9-4 market rival Hatteen for a head success after a late duel between the two lightly-raced three-year-olds.

articles.title: Diamond Necklace sparkles in Nassau Stakes
articles.summary: Diamond Necklace enhanced her reputation even further with a dazzling display to make it six from six in the Group One Nassau Stakes on day two of the Glorious Goodwood Festival.
articles.body:
Diamond Necklace lived up to her billing when extending her unbeaten record with a dominant display in the Qatar Nassau Stakes at Goodwood.

Having rounded off a perfect juvenile campaign with victory in the Prix Marcel Boussac on Arc weekend at ParisLongchamp, Aidan O'Brien's filly has returned to France to secure back-to-back Classic wins this year, in the French 1000 Guineas and French Oaks.

She was the 4-6 favourite to make it six from six as she faced her elders for the first time and while Friendly Soul did her best to shake her off, Ryan Moore always looked ultra-confident in the saddle aboard Diamond Necklace and she pulled two and three-quarter lengths clear with the minimum of fuss.

An impressed Moore said: "That's the best she's felt, she's improving with her racing. Aidan said she was up in her weight a bit today so she's obviously thriving.

  • Scandinavia retains Goodwood Cup crown after eventful race
  • Kalpana defeats Calandagan in King George battle

"She's classy, it was very easy really. She travelled smoothly and quickened up well, she's a little bit idle in front still, but she's a proper racing machine.

"She gives you a classy feel, every time I've ridden her she's travelled with loads of pace, loads of enthusiasm and she has a turn of foot; that's what her father (St Mark's Basilica) had, a real good turn of foot and that's what's evident with her."

O'Brien was delighted to see Diamond Necklace enhance her unbeaten record and said: "She's lovely and she's progressing and she was heavier today, but Rachel (Richardson, work rider) was confident that was just strength she was building rather than just being heavy and it was the way she went through the line.

"There's a lot of people around her who help her and she's a lovely filly. This was a mile and a quarter against older fillies and we didn't know what was going to happen. We put in a lot of pace as we didn't want a Mickey Mouse race and she has options now.

"You can see her quality the way she travels through a race and Ryan was hoping they would lead him longer and he just had to go on as her stride was getting broken. She is a great cruiser and she has a lot of quality and is progressing great so I'm over the moon."

Diamond Necklace was shortened to 8-1 from 14s for the Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe by Paddy Power, but O'Brien is yet to commit on stretching her stamina any further than the 10 furlongs, with the star filly holding a multitude of options for later in the season.

He added: "Constitution River is the boss and everyone has to fall into line behind him. At the moment he is going to York and we're looking forward to that.

"She could stay at a mile and a quarter and go to the race at Leopardstown (Irish Champion Stakes), or France for an Arc trial, she has all those races open to her and she does handle soft ground as well as she handles fast ground.

"The Arc is possibility and she could be a Breeders' Cup filly, it will depend how far we ask her to go. Her next run will tell us where she is going to go and she has a long stride on her and loves nice ground and a fast track, she has a lot of options."

Friendly Soul has endured her fair share of drama since returning from injury this year, being the horse who put a foot in a hole at Haydock before a luckless run in the Duke of Cambridge Stakes at Royal Ascot.

"She's run a fine race against a top class three-year-old who is unbeaten," said Thady Gosden, who trains the five-year-old alongside father John.

"It was a very good effort and we will now in consultation with George and Julia (Strawbridge, owners) look at the programme ahead in which there are some good opportunities for older fillies."

Enceladus impresses in Gordon - but Leger run not set in stone

Joseph O'Brien is keen to keep his options open with Enceladus following his authoritative victory in the Maison Perrier Gordon Stakes at Goodwood.

The Sea The Stars colt has looked much improved since being stepped up in trip this season, with a comeback win at Cork followed by Royal Ascot success in the King George V Stakes.

The William Haggas-trained pair of Desert Hero (2023) and Merchant (2025) won the same Ascot handicap in recent years before landing this Group Three prize and after being sent off a well-backed 6-4 favourite to follow suit, Enceladus finished strongly under Dylan Browne McMonagle, keeping Geryon at bay by a length and a quarter.

Classic sponsors Betfred make Enceladus a 10-1 shot from 25-1 for the Leger, a race which saw O'Brien break his British Classic duck as a trainer with Galileo Chrome six years ago - but the trainer warned he is not certain to head for Doncaster in September.

O'Brien was at Galway rather than Goodwood, from where he told Press Association: "I'm delighted, it was a nice ride from Dylan. It was a really nice performance and he's a progressive, improving colt.

"It was a big step up in class and it's a hard thing to do, but he's going the right way and I'm delighted to have a horse of his potential for Maria and the Niarchos team."

On a Leger bid, he added: "It is one of the more obvious options, but I don't know if we'll rush him past a mile and a half either. Let's see how he pulls up and let the dust settle and we'll lock in his next target after that."

McMonagle said: "He's a lovely, big, straightforward horse. He's done nothing but improve and each run he's getting better.

"I think he's going to be a very nice horse going forward and I do think he's up to that level (Group Twos and Group Ones) with a bit of time.

"As you can see he's still a big baby - when he's getting there he's just doing enough, but he was a good winner.

"He handles that ground well and I think he's got a bit of class - he's a horse to look forward to and one to keep an eye on."

Colin Keane said of the runner-up: "I thought for a few strides that we were going to get to Dylan's horse (Enceladus) but he picked up and went away again.

"I'd say the winner is smart but we're smart as well, he's just a bit of a work in progress. He probably didn't (see it out as well as the winner), but I do think in time he will.

"He's a little hard on himself, he wears earplugs to help him relax so he's a work in progress but a horse with a big future hopefully."

articles.title: American Affair flies the flag for Goldie at Goodwood
articles.summary: American Affair returned to winning ways with a sizzling display in the King George Qatar Stakes on Day Four of Glorious Goodwood, surging to success in the shadows of the post for Jim Goldie and Paul Mulrennan,
articles.body:
Scottish speedball American Affair bounced back to form to claim top honours in the King George Qatar Stakes at Goodwood.

Jim Goldie's stable star won the King Charles III Stakes at Royal Ascot last summer, but missed the remainder of the 2025 season through injury.

A second-place finish behind the reopposing Night Raider in Haydock's Temple Stakes in May suggested he retained a good level of his ability, but having trailed home last of all when defending his Ascot title and since come up short in a Listed race at York, he was a 12-1 shot for his latest Group Two assignment.

Always up with the pace in the group that raced closest to the stands rail, American Affair finished off strongly in the hands of his regular partner Paul Mulrennan to get up and beat Rumstar and Time For Sandals down the middle of the track, with Australian raider Asfoora running her best race for a while in fourth.

  • Former Premier League striker Doyle chasing Cheltenham Festival glory
  • Diamond Necklace sparkles in Nassau Stakes

Goldie senior stayed closer to home, but his son, George, said: "My dad is at Musselburgh, we couldn't both come here, but I think he'll be sorry to have missed out!

"My daughter rides him every day, he's a lovely-natured horse and he's obviously very talented.

"We had faith he'd be back to this level, we've been happy with him at home but things were interrupted by the injury he had at the back end of last year.

"This year it has been a case of building him back up to his best, he showed a glimmer at Haydock three runs ago, but Ascot was a bit of a disaster - he just pulled too hard.

"He ran well at York when he was drawn badly, so we were coming here very hopeful. He's been getting back into that flow of racing properly and finishing his race off.

"We were hoping today was going to suit him better, we were coming here very hopeful."

On future plans, he added: "The plan is to go for the Nunthorpe now, then maybe the Curragh or he could go up to six (furlongs) for the Haydock Sprint Cup.

"We've not entered him in the Abbaye, the Flying Five at the Curragh after the Nunthorpe is more likely."

Weighing-room stalwart Mulrennan said: "He's done everything right today so, touch wood, he comes back from this good. We'll enjoy today, but we've got the Nunthorpe and possibly America would be nice.

"At this stage of the game I've probably got more years behind me than in front of me, but I feel I'm still going strong. It's very competitive, it's hard. I've only got one ride down here this week, but we've made it count.

"I've got my driver with me, Adele (wife). The last time I won it was on Moviesta, Adele drove me then. I've won this race twice and I probably should have won it twice again - Easton Angel probably should have won and Moviesta another year was unlucky, so it's been an unlucky race for me and a lucky race for me, but we got it right today."

Wendy McGrandles of Barraston Racing, who own American Affair with Goldie, said: "He's had one or two excuses and we always felt that he was as good as he was last year. It's once in a lifetime for us, small breeders.

"I remember him as a foal and thinking we could maybe send him eventing if he wasn't fast enough to go racing. He was broken in to go eventing because we weren't sure whether he would be big enough or fast enough to be a racehorse. He can always do that as a second career!"

Burke eyes American trip for Shayem after Thoroughbred success

Karl Burke is eyeing a trip to America with Shayem after he denied the fast-finishing favourite Talk Of New York in the HKJC World Pool Thoroughbred Stakes.

Having finished third behind Wednesday's Sussex Stakes one-two Bow Echo and Gstaad in the St James's Palace at Royal Ascot, this Group Three contest looked a gilt-edged opportunity for Charlie Appleby's Talk Of New York to get back on the winning trail and he was priced up accordingly as the 2-5 market leader.

But while his stablemate Catullus was deployed in a pacemaking role in an attempt to ensure a sound gallop, the favourite was still keen during the early exchanges under William Buick and it then took him a while to find top gear once asked to close the gap.

Karl Burke's Shayem - winner of the Listed Sir Henry Cecil Stakes at Newmarket three weeks ago - was always in the prime position behind Catullus and after grabbing the lead racing inside the final half-furlong, he had enough in hand to keep Talk Of New York at bay by half a length in the hands of Clifford Lee.

"We don't have to lead, but we knew Billy (Loughnane, riding Catullus) was going to go off a nice gallop and Cliff was the only one really to keep tabs on the leader," said Burke.

"Last year, you would have said that he was a soft ground horse but he has proven otherwise this year. We had no qualms about the ground or the track as he handled the undulations at Newmarket well.

"Cliff is very good with his fractions. It was a great performance and Abdulrazaq (Mohamdi, owner) will be delighted as he's a homebred horse as well. He's a great supporter of ours from Dubai.

"There is a nice race at Kentucky Downs for him in September and one at Colonial Downs as well. I don't think they are Grade Ones but they are very valuable races and if if we don't go there, we could come back for the Celebration Mile."

Appleby will let the dust settle on Talk Of New York's disappointing defeat before considering his next move.

He said: "At the top of the hill I thought they'd have to go a bit to go past the lead horse because he's no mug and he likes the track. Stretching to the mile was always going to be the undoing of Catullus - stop the clock a furlong out and we were a comfortable winner.

"William said himself, the front two stole a good march on him and they're two sensible horses. We knew that Catullus was not going to see the mile out eventually but Will said 'I was only just getting rolling there the last furlong'

"I'm not using the track as an excuse, I think the winner is sensible and is improving, he's done everything right, got a nice lead from us and used it, and we've gone and finished the race off.

"You could say do we need to step up in trip? Possibly. But he has got to learn to settle a little bit as well - that first furlong he does want to be a little bit aggressive, but I don't think that was really the undoing of the race to be fair. The pace was on and they weren't coming back at the end of the day."

"We don't have to lead, but we knew Billy (Loughnane, riding Catullus) was going to go off a nice gallop and Cliff was the only one really to keep tabs on the leader," said Burke.

"Last year, you would have said that he was a soft ground horse but he has proven otherwise this year. We had no qualms about the ground or the track as he handled the undulations at Newmarket well.

"Cliff is very good with his fractions. It was a great performance and Abdulrazaq (Mohamdi, owner) will be delighted as he's a homebred horse as well. He's a great supporter of ours from Dubai.

"There is a nice race at Kentucky Downs for him in September and one at Colonial Downs as well. I don't think they are Grade Ones but they are very valuable races and if if we don't go there, we could come back for the Celebration Mile."

Appleby will let the dust settle on Talk Of New York's disappointing defeat before considering his next move.

He said: "At the top of the hill I thought they'd have to go a bit to go past the lead horse because he's no mug and he likes the track. Stretching to the mile was always going to be the undoing of Catullus - stop the clock a furlong out and we were a comfortable winner.

"William said himself, the front two stole a good march on him and they're two sensible horses. We knew that Catullus was not going to see the mile out eventually but Will said 'I was only just getting rolling there the last furlong'

"I'm not using the track as an excuse, I think the winner is sensible and is improving, he's done everything right, got a nice lead from us and used it, and we've gone and finished the race off.

"You could say do we need to step up in trip? Possibly. But he has got to learn to settle a little bit as well - that first furlong he does want to be a little bit aggressive, but I don't think that was really the undoing of the race to be fair. The pace was on and they weren't coming back at the end of the day."

articles.title: Jockey Jim Crowley announces retirement from the saddle due to injury and plans to start training
articles.summary: Having been on the sidelines since a fall at York last September, top rider Jim Crowley announced his retirement on the final day of the Goodwood Festival with plans to start training in 2027
articles.body:
Jim Crowley has called time on his illustrious riding career having failed to recover sufficiently from a serious injury he suffered in a fall at York in September.

Crowley began his time in the saddle as a National Hunt jockey but it was not until he switched to the Flat that he really began to showcase his talent.

He rode his first Group-race winner on Rod Millman's Hawridge Prince in the 2006 Jockey Club Cup but had to wait a further five years before a breakthrough at the highest level on Robert Cowell's Prohibit in the King's Stand at Royal Ascot (now King Charles II Stakes).

He became champion jockey in 2016, after which he was appointed as the retained rider for Hamdan Al Maktoum's Shadwell Stud, when his career hit new heights.

  • Former Premier League striker Doyle chasing Cheltenham Festival glory
  • Diamond Necklace sparkles in Nassau Stakes

Crowley, 48, had the pleasure of riding such champions as Battaash, one of the greatest five-furlong sprinters of the modern era and Baaeed, arguably the best miler since Frankel.

His Shadwell job meant he spent many winters in Dubai where he enjoyed great success, while the likes of Mohaather, Anmaat, Hukum and Ulysses were other top-class horses he will be remembered for.

Unfortunately that day at York has brought his career to a premature end, as following a multitude of operations on his pelvis and legs, he has come to the conclusion that now is the right time for another change of career, as he plans to start training.

Crowley told the Press Association: "I've had an amazing career and to come from jumping and then go on to do as well as I did on the Flat was amazing. I partnered some great horses and it gave me days I could only dream of.

"I never imagined this happening when I came from jumping and I was fortunate to ride all over the world and for some of the best trainers in the world.

"It's been a great career, it's just unfortunate that after my accident at York my body couldn't get back to the level I want to be to race ride again.

"It's nice to announce the retirement at Goodwood. It's my home track and I've had so many good days here and it's nice to finish here."

He went on: "I've always wanted to be a trainer and to train and I think it is the right time for me. It's given me something to get my teeth into. If I could have half as successful training career as I did riding then I would be very happy.

"I've completed my modules and just need to apply for my licence now. I plan on travelling around a bit and spending some time with different trainers and hopefully set up over the winter ahead of next season."

Reflecting on some of his personal highlights from his time in the saddle, it is no surprise Baaeed features heavily.

It is his Queen Elizabeth II Stakes victory at Ascot and then his memorable Juddmonte International romp on his first attempt at 10 furlongs that Crowley remembers most fondly from his time aboard the son of Sea The Stars, thankful to spend the latter stages of his riding career donning the famous Maktoum family silks.

Crowley added: "I've been very privileged and it's thanks to the Maktoum family, Sheikha Hissa and her father who gave me a wonderful opportunity.

"Obviously Baaeed was the best I rode, but there was also Battaash who was by far the best sprinter. There's so many really, Anmaat, Mostahdaf, Hukum who was a great favourite of mine and obviously won the King George, Ulysses, Minzaal - there is so many I've been lucky to ride.

"The day I was made champion jockey was a highlight and so was riding a treble on British Champions Day the day Baaeed beat Palace Pier in the Queen Elizabeth II Stakes.

"Baaeed's Juddmonte Stakes win was another brilliant day, as was Battaash breaking the track record in the Nunthorpe at York."

articles.title: Prix Rothschild: Blue Bolt confirms superiority over Precise in Deauville Group 1
articles.summary: Having been manoeuvred towards the stands-side rail by Colin Keane, Blue Bolt dug deep to deny Precise again in the Group 1 Prix Rothschild at Deauville.
articles.body:
Blue Bolt continued her faultless campaign with victory in the Prix Rothschild at Deauville.

Runner-up to Fallen Angel in the Sun Chariot at Newmarket at the end of last season, Andrew Balding's filly has taken her game to another level this term with a comeback win in Listed company at Goodwood followed by big-race triumphs in the Duke of Cambridge Stakes at Royal Ascot and the Falmouth at Newmarket.

The four-year-old was renewing rivalry with the July course runner-up, Aidan O'Brien's Irish 1,000 Guineas and Coronation Stakes heroine Precise, and at one stage it looked like the latter may take her revenge in the hands of Ryan Moore.

But Blue Bolt was doing her best work at the finish under Colin Keane and lunged late to claim a seventh win from 10 career starts, with Sir Mark Prescott's Coronation Stakes fourth Moon Target bettering that result with a fine effort to finish third.

  • Crowley 'looking forward' to kickstarting training career
  • 'Not good enough!' | Murphy rues Goodwood performance

Balding told Sky Sports Racing: "She's some filly, she really is - and Colin gave her a wonderful ride. It wasn't very comfortable watching it, I thought we were beat in the last furlong, but he's judged it to perfection.

"She's got great physical strength for a filly, that's her biggest quality, and she's got great desire as well. A big thank you to the team at home and Alfie Redman who rides her every day. She's not easy and likes to take control of things, but he's really mastered her this last six months and done a great job of it.

"She likes to get on with it, she's a powerful traveller and knows her strength, so it's about harnessing that in the right direction."

Blue Bolt now looks set to bid for further Group One success in Ireland, with her trainer adding: "The great thing about her is she's effective on any ground, which is a big help.

"We always felt the Matron Stakes at Leopardstown (September 12) was her race this year and we won't lose sight of that for anything prior to that."

articles.title: Shergar Cup: Jamie Lynch's five horses to follow at Ascot on Saturday as international stars battle it out
articles.summary: Sky Sports Racing's senior form analyst Jamie Lynch nominates five runners to note at the Shergar Cup from Ascot on Saturday, all six races are live on Sky Sports Racing; Ryan Moore returns to the team competition for the first time since 2006
articles.body:
The Shergar Cup is back at Ascot this Saturday, with a line-up of international stars, a brand new team and the return of one of the world's best jockeys in Ryan Moore.

1.35 - Dubai Duty Free Shergar Cup Dash (5f)

A fortnight ago at Cork, KENDALL ROY was beaten a short head and a neck in a five-furlong handicap which was sub-57 seconds, and he felt the pinch of that before finishing off strongly, so much so that he could be considered rather lucky to be left on the same mark.

His trainer Kate McGivern is three from nine at home in Ireland this year, and she clearly has a touch with sprinters given Grayrobin's rapid rise. With All Ways Glamorous, Gold Star Hero and Cinque Verde in direct competition, the Dash projects to get very hot very quickly, which will be right up Kendall Roy's fast-finishing street.

2:10 - Dubai Duty Free Shergar Cup Stayers (2m)

Mark Johnston was beaten a short head into second with Spirit of Love in the very first Shergar Cup Stayers event and, a quarter of a century on, the same stable, with Charlie in charge, is still fashioning the same sort.

POLE STAR needs a bounce back, but returning to two miles will help him no end and he's now lower in the handicap than when he won a Racing League race around this time last year.

He maps to be prominent in a race without much pace and, interlinked, he has the acute advantage of Dylan Browne McMonagle, whose stats this season are all the more striking at staying trips, with a 20 per cent strike-rate in Britain and Ireland.

3:20 - Dubai Duty Free Shergar Cup Sprint (6f)

The 2025 Windsor Castle winner HAVANA HURRICANE has only recently dipped down to handicaps, after contesting the Commonwealth Cup, but they've both been over five furlongs, which no longer gets to the bottom of him.

But, he generated the flame symbol for his finish at Sandown and was beaten only two-and-a-half lengths - again after good late work - in a better handicap than this at Ascot last time in which the first two were Dubai Bling and Behike.

The seduction of a straight six means this race, more than any at the Shergar Cup, traditionally goes the way of the hold-up horses (the last six winners have all come from the back of the field), and Havana Hurricane certainly fits that bill.

3:55 - Dubai Duty Free Shergar Cup Classic (1m 4f)

HOSEKI recorded closing splits of 11.9s, 11.3s and 11.5s - rare indeed for this course and distance - when she overcame a steady gallop last month, probably undersold by a 5lb rise.

The other upshot of the pedestrian pace that day is we're still to see much of the stamina that Hoseki is bred for (from the family of Al Aasy and Align The Stars).

She's on a roll, as is her rider Saffie Osborne, and, for many, Hoseki is the make-or-break horse of the 2026 Shergar Cup. I think she'll make it four in a row.

4:30 - Dubai Duty Free Shergar Cup Mile (1m)

At the age of five, 31 races into his career, TWO TRIBES will be trying a mile for the first time here, but his finishing speed and run-out speed from the seven-furlong International - in which he was second (of 16) to Amazing Journey - raises hope for the requisite stamina.

It's easy to hand him a pass for last week when favourite to make it back-to-back Stewards' Cups, as he all but came down leaving the stalls, and, given his gears and late-coming style, the race flow of a round mile at Ascot may just suit him, plus he has McMonagle on board.

articles.title: Hollie Doyle: Expect Thunder Call to play a part in Shergar Cup at Ascot live on Sky Sports Racing on Saturday
articles.summary: Our ambassador Hollie Doyle gives her verdict on the Ascot card with the Shergar Cup taking centre stage on Saturday with Ryan Moore, Christophe Lemaire and Yutaka Take all in action; watch all six races live on Sky Sports Racing
articles.body:
Our ambassador Hollie Doyle, who was the leading rider at the 2023 Shergar Cup, runs the rule over Saturday's international contest at Ascot - live on Sky Sports Racing.

Glamorous can have them singing in the Valleys

It's exciting for Welsh trainer Chris Mason to have a runner in this year's Dubai Duty Free Shergar Cup and they'll be singing loud in his Monmouth village on Saturday night if All Ways Glamorous takes the opening Dubai Duty Free Shergar Cup Dash (1.35) at Ascot.

His five-year-old, who will be representing Team Europe, already has a course-and-distance win to his name after impressing off a five-pound lower rating two weeks ago and can give French rider Marie Velon a great experience.

  • Crowley 'looking forward' to kickstarting training career
  • 'Not good enough!' | Murphy rues Goodwood performance

Europe's Bolo Neighs looks poised to get his head in front soon after flashing home in the same race last time but has work to do to turn the tables, while Ryan Moore can be relied upon to get the best out of my old friend Spartan Arrow who has been working well enough to put points on the board for Great Britain and Ireland.

Shady has Moore to offer in Stayers

Shrimp Shady is a young horse going places and can give Great Britain and Ireland maximum points in the Dubai Duty Free Shergar Cup Stayers (2.10).

Andrew Balding's four-year-old has landed big marathon handicaps at Chester and Newbury already this summer and looks made for this stiff two-mile trip with Ryan Moore set for another plum ride.

Europe, who haven't won the Shergar Cup since back-to-back triumphs in 2013 and 2014, are also well represented with the Ian Williams-trained Hermetic likely to build on his fourth at Newcastle under the classy Christophe Lemaire. This ex-French winner could be well treated off a mark of 81.

Castle in driving seat for Ferraris

It was good to see Richard and Peter Fahey come off the cold list at Southwell on Thursday, just in time for Castle Stuart's run in the Dubai Duty Free Shergar Cup Challenge (2.45).

Hong Kong, who are competing as a team for the first time, have a live contender in this reliable four-year-old who has been unfortunate to bump into two Roger Varian improvers at York this summer. South African Luke Ferraris, a well-known name in China, can be relied upon to get the best out of him.

Ian Williams has the services of Irish champion Dylan Browne McMonagle on his likely favourite Night Breeze, a consistent sort who was a good third at Goodwood but needs a career best to win this, which could make him a shade vulnerable. Insanity took this two years ago for Rachel King and can go well again under Europe's Velon.

Thunder a big player for Hong Kong debutant

Thunder Call didn't appear to enjoy Newmarket's undulations last time but can get back to winning ways for the Hong Kong team in the Dubai Duty Free Shergar Cup Sprint (3.20).

William Haggas' sprinter won in the style of a very nice horse at York before that and promises to be ideally suited to the stiff finish at Ascot, with British racing debutant Jerry Chau on board.

One to watch out for is Great Britain and Ireland's Cape Ashizuri who is unexposed enough to put a disappointing run in a big field last time behind him. John and Sean Quinn will be happy to have McMonagle in the plate.

Archers can hit the target for Ryan

Newmarket-based Italian trainer Marco Botti can put maximum points on the scoreboard for Great Britain and Ireland in the Dubai Duty Free Shergar Cup Classic (3.55).

Archers Bay, another strong chance for Moore, has been bumping into the likes of Ancient Egypt and Heraldry since winning at Newmarket - form that stands out in what doesn't look the strongest renewal.

Team-mate Hoseki is on a roll after rattling up a hat-trick in a course-and-distance fillies' race under a light weight. I'm not sure how much improvement she has left off this five-pound higher mark, though. A more interesting proposition could be Jessie Harrington's Pierre Grosse who is still a maiden but brings solid form to the race in first-time cheekpieces.

Bullet to make a Point in Cup decider

The closing Dubai Duty Free Shergar Cup Mile (4.30) could determine where the trophy goes this year with Europe's Bullet Point the one I expect to capitalise.

Lemaire partners Haggas' gelding, who has the sheepskins on for the first time after not hitting top stride in two starts this year. He is only a pound higher than when he won a big handicap at York's Ebor Festival 12 months ago.

I also like Rest of the World's Ebt's Guard, a course-and-distance winner who has run well in big handicaps at Royal Ascot and Sandown and looks a big player for Indian ace Suraj Narredu, who won the competition with Team Asia last year.

Special memories of the Shergar Cup

The Dubai Duty Free Shergar Cup has given me some of my most special days on a racecourse and I'm excited to watch the action unfold in front of what will once again be a big, enthusiastic crowd at Ascot.

I've been lucky enough to ride three winners in the competition including a double three years ago when I was presented with the Alistair Haggis Silver Saddle Trophy for the highest points scorer.

I was on the winning team in 2023 and 2018 and can tell you that lifting that cup is such a buzz. Being part of a team competition is something we don't often experience as jockeys so the rivalry out on the turf on Saturday will be intense.

I also like Rest of the World's Ebt's Guard, a course-and-distance winner who has run well in big handicaps at Royal Ascot and Sandown and looks a big player for Indian ace Suraj Narredu, who won the competition with Team Asia last year.

Special memories of the Shergar Cup

The Dubai Duty Free Shergar Cup has given me some of my most special days on a racecourse and I'm excited to watch the action unfold in front of what will once again be a big, enthusiastic crowd at Ascot.

I've been lucky enough to ride three winners in the competition including a double three years ago when I was presented with the Alistair Haggis Silver Saddle Trophy for the highest points scorer.

articles.title: Weekend Winners: Kate Tracey, Sam Boswell and Jamie Lynch have their say on Saturday's Shergar Cup Sprint at Ascot
articles.summary: Ahead of another fun-filled Saturday with a typically competitive edition of the Shergar Cup at Ascot, the Weekend Winners team discuss their best bets for the Sprint; watch all six races from Ascot live on Sky Sports Racing
articles.body:
Kate Tracey, Sam Boswell and Jamie Lynch reconvene to discuss the best betting angles for the Shergar Cup Sprint at Ascot on Saturday, live on Sky Sports Racing.

Thunder Call heads the market for this typically competitive heat having gone down on his sword when looking to complete a hat-trick in a hot three-year-old handicap at Newmarket last time out, but all three of our panellists are taking on the William Haggas-trained sprinter.

Senior form analyst Jamie Lynch:

"Quick conditions will help for Havana Hurricane, trained by Eve Johnson Houghton. He's up to six furlongs from five last time and this is only his third handicap start too. He was well liked last year and won the Windsor Castle.

"The key here is up in trip and being held up. The last five winners of this race have come from off the pace as they go a fair gallop. There is a lot to like with him here and he's a proper each-way price."

Host Kate Tracey:

"The horse for me is Figjam, who was second at Doncaster last season in a competitive handicap. She had been pitched into the deep end in the Firth Of Clyde and ran fourth. She makes her handicap debut.

"Her rating could be a little high but the thing with her is she's still so unexposed for a trainer who has done well with sprinting mares this season in Katie Scott. I think she's a lot more unexposed than these and has a good chance here."

BetVictor's Sam Boswell:

"I'm going against the favourite with the John and Sean Quinn-trained Cape Ashizuri who has been chucked into the deep end on a few occasions. He ran in the Champagne Stakes on his second start where he did finish last, but they thought enough of him to pitch him into a Group Two on his second start. He then bumped into Saber Strike who is a good horse in his own right, before flopping at York in a big-field handicap.

"That was only his fifth career start and I'm willing to put a line through it, and he's got Dylan Browne McMonagle jocked up for the first time who is one of the best in the Shergar Cup. The ground should be fine for him and he's a good bet."
